document.content:
{
  "title": "New Hire Orientation & Tooling Playbook",
  "space": "company-handbook",
  "author": "Maya Patel",
  "owner_team": "people-ops",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2024-11-15",
  "last_updated": "2025-02-10",
  "reviewers": [
    "Liam Chen",
    "Rupa Singh",
    "Andre Gomez"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "onboarding",
    "new-hire",
    "tools",
    "people-ops"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "related_pages": [
    "/confluence/company-handbook/00_overview/employee-handbook-2024",
    "/confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/one-click-dev-setup"
  ],
  "content": "Overview:\\n\\nThis playbook is the canonical guide for orienting new hires at Redwood Inference. It combines the people-ops onboarding checklist, role-specific 30/60/90 templates, access provisioning procedures, an internal tools primer, and first-week agenda recommendations. Use this doc to coordinate hiring managers, IT, security, and the new hire so that day 1 is productive and secure.\\n\\nWho this is for:\\n- Hiring managers preparing a new joiner\\n- People Ops coordinators running orientation\\n- IT/Security staff provisioning accounts and devices\\n- New hires who want a single source of truth for the first 90 days\\n\\nGoals:\\n- Ensure all essential accounts and hardware are provisioned by day 1 (target SLA below).\\n- Provide a clear 30/60/90 learning and success plan for common roles.\\n- Standardize tooling orientation so engineers, product, and SREs can ship quickly and securely.\\n\\nQuick links (internal):\\n- People Ops onboarding JIRA: /jira/POPS-ONBOARD\\n- Device procurement form: /tools/device-request\\n- Okta SSO admin: https://okta.redwood.local\\n- Console sandbox: https://console-sandbox.redwood.local\\n\\nOnboarding SLAs (target):\\n| Item | SLA (business days) | Owner |\\n|---|---:|---|\\n| Okta / core SSO account enabled | 1 | People Ops / IT |\\n| GitHub org membership + repo access | 2 | Eng manager / DevOps |\\n| PagerDuty & Datadog alert access | 2 | Eng SRE |\\n| Laptop procurement (if new) | 3-7 | IT procurement |\\n| Security training assigned | 1 | Security |\\n| Full access to Redwood Console (prod sandbox role) | 3 | Platform team |\\n\\nNote: these are targets. Use expedited channel when access will block day-1 work.\\n\\nDay 0-1 Checklist (numbered steps for managers + Ops):\\n1. Confirm start date and arrival window with People Ops.\\n2. Add new hire to People Ops onboarding JIRA and attach signed offer.\\n3. Create Okta account and add to SSO groups (engineering/product/sales as appropriate).\\n4. Request laptop via Device procurement form (include preferred OS, accessories).\\n5. Add to relevant Slack channels, Mail Groups, and Confluence spaces.\\n6. Grant GitHub org membership and base repo access (create PR template if repo requires).\\n7. Assign mandatory trainings: security, privacy, code of conduct (links provided in the People Ops JIRA).\\n8. Schedule 60-minute orientation with People Ops and 30-minute manager check-in for day 1.\\n9. Assign onboarding buddy and create calendar invites for first-week paired sessions.\\n10. Run through initial access verification script (see Access Verification below).\\n\\nAccess Verification (run with new hire on day 1):\\n- Okta SSO login successful\\n- Email access and distribution lists verified\\n- Slack signed in on desktop and mobile\\n- GitHub access to at least 2 repos: onboarding and team repo\\n- Console sandbox access: able to view the \u2018Teams\u2019 dashboard and run a sample request in staging\\n- PagerDuty: able to view on-call rota and acknowledge a test alert\\n- Datadog: able to view sample dashboards and logs\\n\\nFirst-week recommended agenda (sample):\\n- Day 1 morning: People Ops orientation (benefits walkthrough, payroll, policies), office tour or virtual welcome, equipment handoff.\\n- Day 1 afternoon: Team intro, assign buddy, first 1:1 with manager (30m), access verification walkthrough.\\n- Day 2: Codebase orientation (eng), product roadmap overview (product), sales shadow (go-to-market).\\n- Day 3: Security and compliance deep-dive (required), CI/CD demo, sample PR and deploy walkthrough.\\n- Day 4: Start first small onboarding task and pair with buddy.\\n- Day 5: Manager 1:1 + set 30/60/90 objectives.\\n\\n30/60/90 Templates (role-agnostic, editable):\\n- 30 days: Observe, learn internal workflows, complete mandatory trainings, deliver first small task or doc.\\n- 60 days: Own a non-critical feature or process, demonstrate familiarity with primary tools, participate in on-call shadowing if role requires.\\n- 90 days: Independently ship a medium-sized piece of work, present a retrospective on onboarding, and agree on promotion/career goals with manager.\\n\\nRole-specific starters (high level):\\n- Engineering: clone main repos, run local dev with `make dev`, create a test feature branch, complete the runtime onboarding lab in the Console sandbox.\\n- SRE / Platform: validate runbooks, join on-call shadow, perform a canary deploy in staging with telemetry checks.\\n- Product / PM: review 3 recent PRDs, join customer calls, author a small requirement doc and sync with design.\\n- Sales / CS: complete security and data-handling training, shadow enterprise onboarding call, review contract templates and SLA docs.\\n\\nHardware & equipment policy summary:\\n- Standard issue laptop: M1/M2 MacBook Pro (engineering preferred) or equivalent Windows device.\\n- Perks budget for monitors, ergonomic chair reimbursement up to $400.\\n- Replacement lifecycle: 36 months standard; expedited replacement available for critical failures.\\n- Device enrollment: All company devices must be enrolled in MDM and disk encryption enabled.\\n\\nExpense & procurement process (short):\\n1. Fill device/expense request at /tools/device-request.\\n2. Manager approval via JIRA workflow.\\n3. IT issues fulfillment ticket, tracks via procurement board.\\n4. Submit receipts to Expensify under project code REDWOOD-OPS.\\n\\nSecurity and compliance checkpoints (must be completed by end of week 1):\\n- Complete security awareness training.\\n- Confirm MFA is enabled on all accounts.\\n- Sign data handling acknowledgement and NDAs where applicable.\\n- For private deployments or customer-sensitive roles, complete additional onboarding checklist provided by Security (link in People Ops JIRA).\\n\\nInternal tools primer (what to use when):\\n- Slack: informal and synchronous team communication. Use #team-<name>, #all-hands, and private channels for sensitive topics.\\n- Confluence: single source of truth for processes, runbooks, and design docs. Use templates for PRDs and ADRs.\\n- GitHub: code, PR reviews, and issue tracking. Branch naming convention: team/short-desc.\\n- CI/CD: Buildkite for most engineering pipelines; run the `buildkite setup` task in the onboarding lab.\\n- PagerDuty: on-call notifications and escalation. Make sure your local mobile app notifications are enabled.\\n- Datadog: service dashboards, logs, synthetic checks. Dashboards live under `teams/<team-name>`.\\n- Okta: SSO and MFA management. Use Okta to access internal apps.\\n- Vault/KMS: secrets access is role-based and requires requesting a Vault token scoped to projects.\\n- Redwood Console (internal): production and staging routing, model deployments, and telemetry. New hires get read access to sandbox by default; production access is provisioned by manager request.\\n\\nManager responsibilities (short list):\\n- Own the 30/60/90 goals and provide weekly check-ins for the first 90 days.\\n- Assign an onboarding buddy and ensure pairing sessions.\\n- Verify critical access and remove blockers within SLA.\\n- Outline clear success metrics for the first 90 days and review them at week 2 and week 8.\\n\\nBuddy program (how it works):\\n- Buddy length: 6 weeks. Goals: answer day-to-day questions, demo workflows, and provide social context.\\n- Recommended time commitment: 2 hours/week of paired time for the first 3 weeks, then 1 hour/week.\\n\\nCommon onboarding blockers & escalation path:\\n- Missing GitHub access: escalate to DevOps lead and tag #onboarding-help in Slack.\\n- Laptop delivery delay > 7 days: People Ops to escalate to procurement; provide temporary cloud workstation.\\n- Console access failure: open ticket with Platform team and request temporary staging credentials.\\n\\nMeasuring onboarding success (KPIs):\\n- Day-1 access completion rate (target: 95%)\\n- Time-to-first-merge (median) (target: <= 21 days for engineers)\\n- New-hire satisfaction score from 30-day survey (target: >= 4.0/5)\\n\\nAppendix A \u2014 Access request templates (copy into JIRA):\\n- GitHub access request: \\\"Team: <team-name> \u2014 New hire <name> \u2014 Repos: <list> \u2014 Role: write/read\\\"\\n- Console production access request: \\\"New hire <name> \u2014 Customer scope: <customer> \u2014 Justification: <reason> \u2014 Manager approval required\\\"\\n\\nAppendix B \u2014 Sample first ticket for a new engineering hire (copy to repo):\\nTitle: onboarding: hello-world endpoint\\nDescription: Create a small hello-world endpoint that returns service health. Steps: 1) create branch team/onboarding-hello 2) add endpoint and tests 3) open PR with 'onboarding' label 4) assign buddy for review\\n\\nContacts (owners):\\n- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai (Maya Patel)\\n- IT / Procurement: it-ops@redwood.ai (Liam Chen)\\n- Security: security@redwood.ai (Rupa Singh)\\n- Platform access requests: platform-ops@redwood.ai (Andre Gomez)\\n\\nRevision history:\\n- 2024-11-15: Created by Maya Patel (initial playbook).\\n- 2025-02-10: Updated SLAs and added Console sandbox steps (reviewed by Rupa Singh).\\n\\nIf you have feedback or a correction, please use the People Ops onboarding JIRA and tag the document owners above.",

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_92bc3577d2624a9cb294ab827ae60131",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/onboarding-escalation-and-triage-playbook.json",
    "title": "Onboarding Checklist: Support Escalation and Triage Playbook",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Onboarding Checklist: Support Escalation and Triage Playbook\",\n  \"space\": \"customer-success-and-support\",\n  \"author\": \"Dev Patel\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"customer-success\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-03-18\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2025-04-08\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Priya Shah\",\n    \"Sean Gallagher\",\n    \"Logan Wright\",\n    \"Marissa Cole\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"support\",\n    \"onboarding\",\n    \"console\",\n    \"checklist\",\n    \"triage\",\n    \"hosted-api\",\n    \"telemetry\",\n    \"runbook\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"confluence://product-docs/requirements/guided-onboarding-first-production-launch-prd\",\n    \"confluence://architecture-and-standards/api-standards/onboarding-event-schema-v1\",\n    \"confluence://eng-platform/how-tos/checklist-progress-service-integration\",\n    \"confluence://eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/onboarding-kpis-dashboard-spec\",\n    \"confluence://security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/onboarding-telemetry-data-review\",\n    \"confluence://product-docs/release-notes/console-guided-onboarding-checklist-2025-04\"\n  ],\n  \"body\": \"## Purpose\\nThis playbook standardizes how Support and Customer Success (CS) triage onboarding issues for Redwood Hosted API customers using the **Console onboarding checklist** (\\\"Guided onboarding\\\" + \\\"First production launch\\\" checklist).\\n\\nIt covers:\\n- How to interpret checklist state (what it means, what it does *not* mean)\\n- Standard intake questions and what evidence to collect\\n- Common onboarding failures and recommended fixes\\n- When and how to escalate to Console, Platform, Telemetry, SDK, or SRE\\n\\nNon-goals:\\n- This is not a full troubleshooting guide for all API issues.\\n- This does not cover Dedicated/Private onboarding beyond basic pointers.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Audience and assumptions\\n**Primary users:** Support Engineers, CS Engineers, On-call CS.\\n\\nAssumptions:\\n- Customer is using **Hosted API** (unless explicitly noted).\\n- Support has access to Redwood Console support views and internal tooling.\\n- Support can view high-level request metadata (status codes, timestamps, region) but should avoid requesting sensitive data.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Quick definitions\\n**Checklist**: A set of steps surfaced in Console with completion state stored in the Checklist Progress Service.\\n\\n**Step state**:\\n- **Not started**: We have not observed the completion signal.\\n- **In progress**: Partial signals observed (e.g., API key created but no successful request yet).\\n- **Complete**: Completion event(s) observed and accepted.\\n- **Blocked / needs attention** (UI label): Customer likely hit a common failure mode; the system may surface guidance.\\n\\n**Important:** Checklist state is computed from events. A customer can be \\u201cworking correctly\\u201d even if a step is incomplete due to telemetry delay or missing instrumentation.\\n\\n**TTFS / TTFP**:\\n- **TTFS (Time to First Success)**: time from signup to first successful (2xx) API response for an eligible endpoint.\\n- **TTFP (Time to First Production)**: time from signup to first sustained production traffic (as defined in the metrics spec).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Where to find checklist state (Support workflow)\\n1) Open the customer\\u2019s **Console tenant**.\\n2) Navigate to: **Onboarding \\u2192 Checklist** (or the checklist card on the Console home page).\\n3) If available, open **Support View** (shows timestamps and event source metadata).\\n4) If the customer is on a call, confirm they are looking at the **same tenant/workspace** (many issues are \\u201cwrong org/workspace\\u201d).\\n\\nWhat to capture in the ticket:\\n- Tenant/workspace ID\\n- Checklist step names + states (screenshot or copy/paste)\\n- Timestamp of last observed checklist update\\n- Customer-reported time of last attempted action (e.g., \\u201csent request 10 minutes ago\\u201d)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Interpreting checklist state: do\\u2019s and don\\u2019ts\\n### Do\\n- Use the checklist as a **structured interview**: it narrows the likely failure mode.\\n- Cross-check with request metadata: recent status codes, request counts, regions.\\n- Treat steps as **signals**, not as ground truth.\\n\\n### Don\\u2019t\\n- Don\\u2019t ask for customer prompts, full payloads, or raw logs unless required and approved.\\n- Don\\u2019t mark steps complete manually unless (a) you\\u2019ve validated success via internal signals or (b) you are unblocking a UI issue and leaving an audit note.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Standard intake questions (ask in this order)\\nUse these as macros in tickets and live troubleshooting.\\n\\n### A) Account / project alignment\\n1. Which **workspace/tenant** are you using? (Ask for org/workspace name as shown in Console.)\\n2. Which **API key** are you using (name/label, not the full secret)? When was it created?\\n3. Where are you setting the key (env var name, secret manager, CI/CD)?\\n\\n### B) Request details (minimal)\\n4. Which SDK/language and version are you using? (e.g., Python SDK vX.Y, TS SDK vX.Y, OpenAI-compat)\\n5. Which endpoint are you calling? (chat, completions, embeddings)\\n6. Region/edge: which base URL/region are you targeting?\\n7. What error are you seeing (status code + error message string)?\\n\\n### C) Production readiness context\\n8. Are you testing streaming? If yes, what client environment (browser/node/server) and how are you consuming the stream?\\n9. Have you configured retries/timeouts?\\n10. Are you seeing 429s? If yes: expected request rate and concurrency.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Common failures mapped to checklist steps\\nThe table below maps top onboarding ticket categories to likely checklist step states and fixes.\\n\\n| Symptom / Ticket theme | Likely checklist step(s) | Fast diagnosis | Recommended fix | Escalate when |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| 401/403 \\u201cInvalid API key\\u201d / auth failure | \\u201cCreate API key\\u201d complete but \\u201cFirst successful request\\u201d not complete | Wrong workspace, wrong env var name, using revoked key, OpenAI-compat key header mismatch | Verify tenant, re-create key, ensure correct env var, confirm header format per SDK | If correct key still fails with consistent 403 across regions (Platform/Auth) |\\n| First request \\u201cworks\\u201d but checklist doesn\\u2019t update | \\u201cFirst successful request\\u201d not complete | Telemetry delay, request routed via non-instrumented path, tenant mismatch | Wait 5\\u201310 minutes; confirm request hit Hosted gateway; verify correct org | If >30 minutes delay with verified 2xx requests (Telemetry) |\\n| Streaming disconnect confusion / partial output | \\u201cStreaming response\\u201d incomplete or flagged | Client not reading stream properly, idle timeout, missing reconnect logic | Use SDK streaming helper; ensure keep-alive; implement reconnect/backoff | If consistent disconnect at same server timestamp across customers/regions (SRE/Platform) |\\n| Immediate 429 after launch | \\u201cQuotas & rate limits\\u201d incomplete or flagged | Concurrency too high, burst traffic, missing backoff | Configure backoff + retry; adjust quotas; recommend Dedicated for predictable throughput | If 429s occur well below configured quota or inconsistent quota enforcement (Platform/Metering) |\\n| Usage dashboard mismatch / \\u201crequests aren\\u2019t counted\\u201d | \\u201cView usage dashboard\\u201d incomplete/flagged | Dashboard freshness delay, wrong time range/filters, multiple orgs | Explain freshness window; check usage dataset lag; confirm correct filters | If freshness SLA breached or lag spikes (Telemetry/Data Eng) |\\n| Model changes / unexpected behavior post-launch | \\u201cPin model version\\u201d incomplete | Using floating alias, not pinned version, mismatch between environments | Pin model version; set fallback policy | If pinned version still routes unexpectedly (Control Plane) |\\n| Retrying causes duplicate side effects | \\u201cRetries & timeouts\\u201d incomplete | Non-idempotent operations, missing idempotency keys | Add idempotency keys and safe retry policy | If SDK helper seems broken or headers dropped (SDK team) |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Step-by-step triage by checklist section\\n### 1) API key creation & environment setup\\n**What completion means:** An API key was created in Console (or via admin provisioning).\\n\\nTroubleshooting:\\n1. Confirm customer is in the expected workspace.\\n2. Confirm they are using a currently active key (not deleted/rotated).\\n3. Verify the environment variable name used in docs for their SDK.\\n4. For OpenAI-compat usage: confirm base URL and auth header naming per our compatibility layer.\\n\\nEscalation criteria:\\n- Multiple customers reporting 401/403 with newly created keys in the same hour.\\n- Auth failures occur across multiple keys and workspaces with no configuration mistakes.\\n\\nEscalate to: **Platform/Auth** (Kaitlyn Nguyen) and **SRE** if widespread.\\n\\n### 2) First successful API call (TTFS)\\n**What completion means:** We observed the first eligible 2xx response from the Hosted gateway for the tenant.\\n\\nTroubleshooting:\\n1. Ask for a timestamp of their last attempt.\\n2. Check internal request metadata for 2xx vs 4xx/5xx.\\n3. If they are using a local proxy, confirm requests actually reach Hosted.\\n4. If they are using a different org in CI vs local, reconcile workspace IDs.\\n\\nIf checklist is not updating:\\n- Confirm the request hit an instrumented gateway path.\\n- Allow for telemetry lag (up to 10 minutes is typical).\\n\\nEscalation criteria:\\n- Verified 2xx requests with no checklist update after 30 minutes.\\n\\nEscalate to: **Telemetry** (Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman).\\n\\n### 3) Streaming enabled\\n**What completion means:** We observed at least one successful streaming session establishment (not necessarily full completion).\\n\\nCommon customer misunderstandings:\\n- They expect streaming to retry automatically.\\n- They treat a client disconnect as a server failure.\\n\\nSupport guidance (production-safe defaults):\\n- Recommend explicit timeouts.\\n- Implement reconnect/backoff on transient errors.\\n- Ensure stream consumer drains events and closes properly.\\n\\nEscalation criteria:\\n- Consistent disconnect patterns at server side across regions.\\n- Elevated stream error rates correlating with incident signals.\\n\\nEscalate to: **SRE** and **Gateway/Serving** on-call; include region and timestamps.\\n\\n### 4) Retries, timeouts, and idempotency\\n**What completion means:** The customer has acknowledged/visited guidance; we may also observe SDK hint headers (where available).\\n\\nSupport checklist:\\n- Verify they are not using infinite retries.\\n- Verify exponential backoff with jitter for 429/5xx.\\n- Encourage idempotency keys for retried requests that trigger side effects downstream.\\n\\nEscalation criteria:\\n- SDK defaults appear wrong or inconsistent with docs.\\n\\nEscalate to: **SDK team** (Monica Patel / Ibrahim Khan).\\n\\n### 5) Quotas, budgets, and rate limits\\n**What completion means:** They viewed quota settings and/or configured an alert/budget.\\n\\nTriage steps for 429:\\n1. Confirm the quota limits visible in Console.\\n2. Ask for peak RPS and concurrency.\\n3. Check whether 429s align with bursts.\\n4. Ensure they have backoff configured.\\n\\nEscalation criteria:\\n- 429 occurs below configured quota or quota changes not applying.\\n\\nEscalate to: **Metering/Quotas** (Cole Summers) and **Telemetry** if enforcement vs reporting mismatch.\\n\\n### 6) Usage dashboard and billing alignment\\n**What completion means:** They visited usage dashboards; does not guarantee they understand freshness windows.\\n\\nKey guidance to provide:\\n- Usage dashboards are near-real-time but can lag (communicate current freshness SLA displayed in Console).\\n- Ensure correct workspace, time range, and environment filters.\\n\\nEscalation criteria:\\n- Freshness lag exceeds SLA or discrepancy persists beyond normal windows.\\n\\nEscalate to: **Telemetry/Data Eng** (Mei Lin) with screenshots and timestamps.\\n\\n### 7) Model pinning and fallback policy (first production launch)\\n**What completion means:** They pinned a model version and configured a fallback policy.\\n\\nTriage prompts:\\n- Are they using a floating alias?\\n- Did they configure fallback across regions or to a compatible model variant?\\n- Are they seeing unexpected model IDs in responses?\\n\\nEscalation criteria:\\n- Control plane displays correct config but gateway routes differently.\\n\\nEscalate to: **Control Plane/Config** (Ethan Park / Benji Okafor).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Escalation routing and required evidence\\n### Severity guidance (Support)\\n- **Sev 1 (Production down):** Customer cannot serve production traffic due to a Redwood-side issue (widespread or confirmed service degradation). Engage SRE immediately.\\n- **Sev 2 (Major impact):** Customer blocked from launching / significant traffic impaired; workaround not available.\\n- **Sev 3 (Standard onboarding issue):** Misconfiguration, docs confusion, or expected limits.\\n\\n### Escalation checklist (include in ticket)\\nWhen escalating, include:\\n- Tenant/workspace ID\\n- Region(s)\\n- Approx timestamps (UTC) of failures/successes\\n- Endpoint (chat/embeddings/etc.)\\n- Status codes distribution (e.g., 401 vs 429 vs 5xx)\\n- Checklist step states + last update time\\n- SDK/language + version\\n- Whether issue reproduces across keys and environments\\n\\n### Team routing\\n- **Console checklist UI issues (missing card, broken deep links, step drawer bugs):** Console team (Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin). Provide browser + Console build version.\\n- **Checklist state wrong / delayed / inconsistent:** Telemetry + Checklist Progress Service owners (Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman). Provide event timestamps and any evidence of out-of-order behavior.\\n- **Auth/API key problems:** Platform/Auth (Kaitlyn Nguyen). Provide key creation time and error strings.\\n- **Quota enforcement vs UI mismatch:** Metering/Quotas (Cole Summers) + Telemetry.\\n- **Routing/model pinning/fallback issues:** Control Plane/Config (Ethan Park / Benji Okafor).\\n- **Widespread errors / suspected incident:** SRE on-call (Sean Gallagher\\u2019s org). Provide region and error rates.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Admin override: when to use and how to document\\nSupport can use admin override tools to mark steps complete/reset **only** in the following cases:\\n- **UI is blocking the customer** (e.g., checklist gating a UI panel) and Support has verified the underlying action succeeded by other signals.\\n- **Telemetry gap** prevents a correct completion state and the customer needs to proceed immediately.\\n- **Customer requests a reset** for training/demo purposes (rare; ensure it\\u2019s the correct tenant and authorized).\\n\\nRules:\\n- Always add an audit note with: reason, evidence source, and the customer contact.\\n- Do not use override to \\u201chide\\u201d genuine failures.\\n\\nSuggested audit note template:\\n- Reason:\\n- Evidence (timestamp, request metadata, screenshot, etc.):\\n- Action taken (mark complete / reset):\\n- Support agent:\\n\\nEscalate before overriding if:\\n- You suspect a systemic telemetry regression.\\n- Overrides are needed repeatedly for multiple customers.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Data handling and privacy\\n- Do not request or store customer prompts, full request bodies, or model outputs in Support tickets unless explicitly approved for that case.\\n- Collect only metadata necessary to debug (timestamps, status codes, tenant ID, SDK version).\\n- Checklist and onboarding telemetry are designed to be **PII-free**; if you observe PII in an event payload or UI surface, treat as a potential security issue and escalate to Security (Marcus Lin) immediately.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Appendix A: Known limitations (as of April 2025 release)\\n- Checklist completion can lag behind real actions due to ingestion delays.\\n- Some integrations (older SDKs, custom gateways) may not emit client hint tags; server-side events should still cover core steps.\\n- Out-of-order event arrival has been observed in dogfood; race-condition fixes are in place, but anomalies may persist in edge cases.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Appendix B: Support macros (copy/paste)\\n### Macro: Request minimal debugging info\\n\\u201cCan you share (1) workspace/org name as shown in Console, (2) which SDK/language + version, (3) the endpoint you\\u2019re calling, and (4) the status code + error message text? If you can include the timestamp (UTC) of your last attempt, we can check our side quickly.\\u201d\\n\\n### Macro: Usage dashboard freshness\\n\\u201cUsage can take a short time to appear in the dashboard depending on ingestion. Please confirm you\\u2019re viewing the correct workspace and time range. If it\\u2019s been >30 minutes since your last successful requests and usage still shows 0, we\\u2019ll investigate telemetry freshness.\\u201d\\n\\n### Macro: 429 guidance\\n\\u201cA 429 indicates you\\u2019re hitting a rate/concurrency limit. The recommended approach is exponential backoff with jitter, plus configuring quotas/budgets in Console to match expected traffic. If you share your approximate concurrency and request rate, we can recommend a safe configuration.\\u201d\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Change log\\n- 2025-04-08: Added escalation evidence checklist; clarified override rules; updated routing owners.\\n- 2025-03-18: Initial version for checklist cohort rollout.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_92bc3577d2624a9cb294ab827ae60131\"\n}",

{
  "title": "Onboarding Checklist: Support Escalation and Triage Playbook",
  "space": "customer-success-and-support",
  "author": "Dev Patel",
  "owner_team": "customer-success",
  "status": "published",
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "created_at": "2025-03-18",
  "last_updated": "2025-04-08",
  "reviewers": [
    "Priya Shah",
    "Sean Gallagher",
    "Logan Wright",
    "Marissa Cole"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "support",
    "onboarding",
    "console",
    "checklist",
    "triage",
    "hosted-api",
    "telemetry",
    "runbook"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "confluence://product-docs/requirements/guided-onboarding-first-production-launch-prd",
    "confluence://architecture-and-standards/api-standards/onboarding-event-schema-v1",
    "confluence://eng-platform/how-tos/checklist-progress-service-integration",
    "confluence://eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/onboarding-kpis-dashboard-spec",
    "confluence://security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/onboarding-telemetry-data-review",
    "confluence://product-docs/release-notes/console-guided-onboarding-checklist-2025-04"
  ],
  "body": "## Purpose
This playbook standardizes how Support and Customer Success (CS) triage onboarding issues for Redwood Hosted API customers using the **Console onboarding checklist** ("Guided onboarding" + "First production launch" checklist).

It covers:
- How to interpret checklist state (what it means, what it does *not* mean)
- Standard intake questions and what evidence to collect
- Common onboarding failures and recommended fixes
- When and how to escalate to Console, Platform, Telemetry, SDK, or SRE

Non-goals:
- This is not a full troubleshooting guide for all API issues.
- This does not cover Dedicated/Private onboarding beyond basic pointers.

---

## Audience and assumptions
**Primary users:** Support Engineers, CS Engineers, On-call CS.

Assumptions:
- Customer is using **Hosted API** (unless explicitly noted).
- Support has access to Redwood Console support views and internal tooling.
- Support can view high-level request metadata (status codes, timestamps, region) but should avoid requesting sensitive data.

---

## Quick definitions
**Checklist**: A set of steps surfaced in Console with completion state stored in the Checklist Progress Service.

**Step state**:
- **Not started**: We have not observed the completion signal.
- **In progress**: Partial signals observed (e.g., API key created but no successful request yet).
- **Complete**: Completion event(s) observed and accepted.
- **Blocked / needs attention** (UI label): Customer likely hit a common failure mode; the system may surface guidance.

**Important:** Checklist state is computed from events. A customer can be “working correctly” even if a step is incomplete due to telemetry delay or missing instrumentation.

**TTFS / TTFP**:
- **TTFS (Time to First Success)**: time from signup to first successful (2xx) API response for an eligible endpoint.
- **TTFP (Time to First Production)**: time from signup to first sustained production traffic (as defined in the metrics spec).

---

## Where to find checklist state (Support workflow)
1) Open the customer’s **Console tenant**.
2) Navigate to: **Onboarding → Checklist** (or the checklist card on the Console home page).
3) If available, open **Support View** (shows timestamps and event source metadata).
4) If the customer is on a call, confirm they are looking at the **same tenant/workspace** (many issues are “wrong org/workspace”).

What to capture in the ticket:
- Tenant/workspace ID
- Checklist step names + states (screenshot or copy/paste)
- Timestamp of last observed checklist update
- Customer-reported time of last attempted action (e.g., “sent request 10 minutes ago”)

---

## Interpreting checklist state: do’s and don’ts
### Do
- Use the checklist as a **structured interview**: it narrows the likely failure mode.
- Cross-check with request metadata: recent status codes, request counts, regions.
- Treat steps as **signals**, not as ground truth.

### Don’t
- Don’t ask for customer prompts, full payloads, or raw logs unless required and approved.
- Don’t mark steps complete manually unless (a) you’ve validated success via internal signals or (b) you are unblocking a UI issue and leaving an audit note.

---

## Standard intake questions (ask in this order)
Use these as macros in tickets and live troubleshooting.

### A) Account / project alignment
1. Which **workspace/tenant** are you using? (Ask for org/workspace name as shown in Console.)
2. Which **API key** are you using (name/label, not the full secret)? When was it created?
3. Where are you setting the key (env var name, secret manager, CI/CD)?

### B) Request details (minimal)
4. Which SDK/language and version are you using? (e.g., Python SDK vX.Y, TS SDK vX.Y, OpenAI-compat)
5. Which endpoint are you calling? (chat, completions, embeddings)
6. Region/edge: which base URL/region are you targeting?
7. What error are you seeing (status code + error message string)?

### C) Production readiness context
8. Are you testing streaming? If yes, what client environment (browser/node/server) and how are you consuming the stream?
9. Have you configured retries/timeouts?
10. Are you seeing 429s? If yes: expected request rate and concurrency.

---

## Common failures mapped to checklist steps
The table below maps top onboarding ticket categories to likely checklist step states and fixes.

| Symptom / Ticket theme | Likely checklist step(s) | Fast diagnosis | Recommended fix | Escalate when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 401/403 “Invalid API key” / auth failure | “Create API key” complete but “First successful request” not complete | Wrong workspace, wrong env var name, using revoked key, OpenAI-compat key header mismatch | Verify tenant, re-create key, ensure correct env var, confirm header format per SDK | If correct key still fails with consistent 403 across regions (Platform/Auth) |
| First request “works” but checklist doesn’t update | “First successful request” not complete | Telemetry delay, request routed via non-instrumented path, tenant mismatch | Wait 5–10 minutes; confirm request hit Hosted gateway; verify correct org | If >30 minutes delay with verified 2xx requests (Telemetry) |
| Streaming disconnect confusion / partial output | “Streaming response” incomplete or flagged | Client not reading stream properly, idle timeout, missing reconnect logic | Use SDK streaming helper; ensure keep-alive; implement reconnect/backoff | If consistent disconnect at same server timestamp across customers/regions (SRE/Platform) |
| Immediate 429 after launch | “Quotas & rate limits” incomplete or flagged | Concurrency too high, burst traffic, missing backoff | Configure backoff + retry; adjust quotas; recommend Dedicated for predictable throughput | If 429s occur well below configured quota or inconsistent quota enforcement (Platform/Metering) |
| Usage dashboard mismatch / “requests aren’t counted” | “View usage dashboard” incomplete/flagged | Dashboard freshness delay, wrong time range/filters, multiple orgs | Explain freshness window; check usage dataset lag; confirm correct filters | If freshness SLA breached or lag spikes (Telemetry/Data Eng) |
| Model changes / unexpected behavior post-launch | “Pin model version” incomplete | Using floating alias, not pinned version, mismatch between environments | Pin model version; set fallback policy | If pinned version still routes unexpectedly (Control Plane) |
| Retrying causes duplicate side effects | “Retries & timeouts” incomplete | Non-idempotent operations, missing idempotency keys | Add idempotency keys and safe retry policy | If SDK helper seems broken or headers dropped (SDK team) |

---

## Step-by-step triage by checklist section
### 1) API key creation & environment setup
**What completion means:** An API key was created in Console (or via admin provisioning).

Troubleshooting:
1. Confirm customer is in the expected workspace.
2. Confirm they are using a currently active key (not deleted/rotated).
3. Verify the environment variable name used in docs for their SDK.
4. For OpenAI-compat usage: confirm base URL and auth header naming per our compatibility layer.

Escalation criteria:
- Multiple customers reporting 401/403 with newly created keys in the same hour.
- Auth failures occur across multiple keys and workspaces with no configuration mistakes.

Escalate to: **Platform/Auth** (Kaitlyn Nguyen) and **SRE** if widespread.

### 2) First successful API call (TTFS)
**What completion means:** We observed the first eligible 2xx response from the Hosted gateway for the tenant.

Troubleshooting:
1. Ask for a timestamp of their last attempt.
2. Check internal request metadata for 2xx vs 4xx/5xx.
3. If they are using a local proxy, confirm requests actually reach Hosted.
4. If they are using a different org in CI vs local, reconcile workspace IDs.

If checklist is not updating:
- Confirm the request hit an instrumented gateway path.
- Allow for telemetry lag (up to 10 minutes is typical).

Escalation criteria:
- Verified 2xx requests with no checklist update after 30 minutes.

Escalate to: **Telemetry** (Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman).

### 3) Streaming enabled
**What completion means:** We observed at least one successful streaming session establishment (not necessarily full completion).

Common customer misunderstandings:
- They expect streaming to retry automatically.
- They treat a client disconnect as a server failure.

Support guidance (production-safe defaults):
- Recommend explicit timeouts.
- Implement reconnect/backoff on transient errors.
- Ensure stream consumer drains events and closes properly.

Escalation criteria:
- Consistent disconnect patterns at server side across regions.
- Elevated stream error rates correlating with incident signals.

Escalate to: **SRE** and **Gateway/Serving** on-call; include region and timestamps.

### 4) Retries, timeouts, and idempotency
**What completion means:** The customer has acknowledged/visited guidance; we may also observe SDK hint headers (where available).

Support checklist:
- Verify they are not using infinite retries.
- Verify exponential backoff with jitter for 429/5xx.
- Encourage idempotency keys for retried requests that trigger side effects downstream.

Escalation criteria:
- SDK defaults appear wrong or inconsistent with docs.

Escalate to: **SDK team** (Monica Patel / Ibrahim Khan).

### 5) Quotas, budgets, and rate limits
**What completion means:** They viewed quota settings and/or configured an alert/budget.

Triage steps for 429:
1. Confirm the quota limits visible in Console.
2. Ask for peak RPS and concurrency.
3. Check whether 429s align with bursts.
4. Ensure they have backoff configured.

Escalation criteria:
- 429 occurs below configured quota or quota changes not applying.

Escalate to: **Metering/Quotas** (Cole Summers) and **Telemetry** if enforcement vs reporting mismatch.

### 6) Usage dashboard and billing alignment
**What completion means:** They visited usage dashboards; does not guarantee they understand freshness windows.

Key guidance to provide:
- Usage dashboards are near-real-time but can lag (communicate current freshness SLA displayed in Console).
- Ensure correct workspace, time range, and environment filters.

Escalation criteria:
- Freshness lag exceeds SLA or discrepancy persists beyond normal windows.

Escalate to: **Telemetry/Data Eng** (Mei Lin) with screenshots and timestamps.

### 7) Model pinning and fallback policy (first production launch)
**What completion means:** They pinned a model version and configured a fallback policy.

Triage prompts:
- Are they using a floating alias?
- Did they configure fallback across regions or to a compatible model variant?
- Are they seeing unexpected model IDs in responses?

Escalation criteria:
- Control plane displays correct config but gateway routes differently.

Escalate to: **Control Plane/Config** (Ethan Park / Benji Okafor).

---

## Escalation routing and required evidence
### Severity guidance (Support)
- **Sev 1 (Production down):** Customer cannot serve production traffic due to a Redwood-side issue (widespread or confirmed service degradation). Engage SRE immediately.
- **Sev 2 (Major impact):** Customer blocked from launching / significant traffic impaired; workaround not available.
- **Sev 3 (Standard onboarding issue):** Misconfiguration, docs confusion, or expected limits.

### Escalation checklist (include in ticket)
When escalating, include:
- Tenant/workspace ID
- Region(s)
- Approx timestamps (UTC) of failures/successes
- Endpoint (chat/embeddings/etc.)
- Status codes distribution (e.g., 401 vs 429 vs 5xx)
- Checklist step states + last update time
- SDK/language + version
- Whether issue reproduces across keys and environments

### Team routing
- **Console checklist UI issues (missing card, broken deep links, step drawer bugs):** Console team (Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin). Provide browser + Console build version.
- **Checklist state wrong / delayed / inconsistent:** Telemetry + Checklist Progress Service owners (Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman). Provide event timestamps and any evidence of out-of-order behavior.
- **Auth/API key problems:** Platform/Auth (Kaitlyn Nguyen). Provide key creation time and error strings.
- **Quota enforcement vs UI mismatch:** Metering/Quotas (Cole Summers) + Telemetry.
- **Routing/model pinning/fallback issues:** Control Plane/Config (Ethan Park / Benji Okafor).
- **Widespread errors / suspected incident:** SRE on-call (Sean Gallagher’s org). Provide region and error rates.

---

## Admin override: when to use and how to document
Support can use admin override tools to mark steps complete/reset **only** in the following cases:
- **UI is blocking the customer** (e.g., checklist gating a UI panel) and Support has verified the underlying action succeeded by other signals.
- **Telemetry gap** prevents a correct completion state and the customer needs to proceed immediately.
- **Customer requests a reset** for training/demo purposes (rare; ensure it’s the correct tenant and authorized).

Rules:
- Always add an audit note with: reason, evidence source, and the customer contact.
- Do not use override to “hide” genuine failures.

Suggested audit note template:
- Reason:
- Evidence (timestamp, request metadata, screenshot, etc.):
- Action taken (mark complete / reset):
- Support agent:

Escalate before overriding if:
- You suspect a systemic telemetry regression.
- Overrides are needed repeatedly for multiple customers.

---

## Data handling and privacy
- Do not request or store customer prompts, full request bodies, or model outputs in Support tickets unless explicitly approved for that case.
- Collect only metadata necessary to debug (timestamps, status codes, tenant ID, SDK version).
- Checklist and onboarding telemetry are designed to be **PII-free**; if you observe PII in an event payload or UI surface, treat as a potential security issue and escalate to Security (Marcus Lin) immediately.

---

## Appendix A: Known limitations (as of April 2025 release)
- Checklist completion can lag behind real actions due to ingestion delays.
- Some integrations (older SDKs, custom gateways) may not emit client hint tags; server-side events should still cover core steps.
- Out-of-order event arrival has been observed in dogfood; race-condition fixes are in place, but anomalies may persist in edge cases.

---

## Appendix B: Support macros (copy/paste)
### Macro: Request minimal debugging info
“Can you share (1) workspace/org name as shown in Console, (2) which SDK/language + version, (3) the endpoint you’re calling, and (4) the status code + error message text? If you can include the timestamp (UTC) of your last attempt, we can check our side quickly.”

### Macro: Usage dashboard freshness
“Usage can take a short time to appear in the dashboard depending on ingestion. Please confirm you’re viewing the correct workspace and time range. If it’s been >30 minutes since your last successful requests and usage still shows 0, we’ll investigate telemetry freshness.”

### Macro: 429 guidance
“A 429 indicates you’re hitting a rate/concurrency limit. The recommended approach is exponential backoff with jitter, plus configuring quotas/budgets in Console to match expected traffic. If you share your approximate concurrency and request rate, we can recommend a safe configuration.”

---

## Change log
- 2025-04-08: Added escalation evidence checklist; clarified override rules; updated routing owners.
- 2025-03-18: Initial version for checklist cohort rollout.",

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/codebase/litellm",
    "content": "# Contributing to LiteLLM\n\nThank you for your interest in contributing to LiteLLM! We welcome contributions of all kinds - from bug fixes and documentation improvements to new features and integrations.\n\n## **Checklist before submitting a PR**\n\nHere are the core requirements for any PR submitted to LiteLLM:\n\n- [ ] **Sign the Contributor License Agreement (CLA)** - [see details](#contributor-license-agreement-cla)\n- [ ] **Keep scope isolated** - Your changes should address 1 specific problem at a time\n\n#### Proxy (Backend) PRs\n\n- [ ] **Add testing** - Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement - [see details](#adding-testing)\n- [ ] **Ensure your PR passes all checks**:\n  - [ ] [Unit Tests](#running-unit-tests) - `make test-unit`\n  - [ ] [Linting / Formatting](#running-linting-and-formatting-checks) - `make lint`\n\n#### UI PRs\n\n- [ ] **Ensure the UI builds successfully** - `npm run build`\n- [ ] **Ensure all UI unit tests pass** - `npm run test`\n- [ ] **Add tests for new components or logic** - If you are adding a new component or new logic, add corresponding tests\n\n## **Contributor License Agreement (CLA)**\n\nBefore contributing code to LiteLLM, you must sign our [Contributor License Agreement (CLA)](https://cla-assistant.io/BerriAI/litellm). This is a legal requirement for all contributions to be merged into the main repository.\n\n**Important:** We strongly recommend reviewing and signing the CLA before starting work on your contribution to avoid any delays in the PR process.\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### 1. Setup Your Local Development Environment\n\n```bash\n# Fork the repository on GitHub (click the Fork button at https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm)\n# Then clone your fork locally\ngit clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/litellm.git\ncd litellm\n\n# Create a new branch for your feature (see \"Commit and Branch Conventions\" below)\ngit checkout -b feature/your-feature\n\n# Install development dependencies\nmake install-dev\n\n# Install git hooks that enforce commit + branch conventions (one-time, opt-in)\nmake install-hooks\n\n# Verify your setup works\nmake help\n```\n\nThat's it! Your local development environment is ready.\n\n## Commit and Branch Conventions\n\nCommits follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) and branches follow [Conventional Branches](https://conventional-branch.github.io/). Run `make install-hooks` once per clone to enable the local git hooks that enforce these — see the [contributor docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code#commit-and-branch-conventions) for the full type list, examples, the protected-branch bypass list, and how to opt out.\n\n### 2. Development Workflow\n\nHere's the recommended workflow for making changes:\n\n```bash\n# Make your changes to the code\n# ...\n\n# Format your code (auto-fixes formatting issues)\nmake format\n\n# Run all linting checks (matches CI exactly)\nmake lint\n\n# Run unit tests to ensure nothing is broken\nmake test-unit\n\n# Commit your changes (must follow Conventional Commits — see above)\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"feat(scope): your descriptive commit message\"\n\n# Push and create a PR (branch must follow Conventional Branches — see above)\ngit push origin feature/your-feature\n```\n\n## Adding Testing\n\n**Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement for all PRs.**\n\n### Where to Add Tests\n\nAdd your tests to the [`tests/test_litellm/` directory](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/test_litellm).\n\n- This directory mirrors the structure of the `litellm/` directory\n- **Only add mocked tests** - no real LLM API calls in this directory\n- For integration tests with real APIs, use the appropriate test directories\n\n### File Naming Convention\n\nThe `tests/test_litellm/` directory follows the same structure as `litellm/`:\n\n- `litellm/proxy/caching_routes.py` → `tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_caching_routes.py`\n- `litellm/utils.py` → `tests/test_litellm/test_utils.py`\n\n### Example Test\n\n```python\nimport pytest\nfrom litellm import completion\n\ndef test_your_feature():\n    \"\"\"Test your feature with a descriptive docstring.\"\"\"\n    # Arrange\n    messages = [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Hello\"}]\n    \n    # Act\n    # Use mocked responses, not real API calls\n    \n    # Assert\n    assert expected_result == actual_result\n```\n\n## Running Tests and Checks\n\n### Running Unit Tests\n\nRun all unit tests (uses parallel execution for speed):\n\n```bash\nmake test-unit\n```\n\nIf you're running broader test suites, proxy tests, or anything that touches PostgreSQL-backed fixtures/plugins, install the full local test environment first:\n\n```bash\nmake install-test-deps\n```\n\nThis syncs the locked test environment used across the repo, including `psycopg` v3 plus `psycopg-binary` (used by `pytest-postgresql`), `psycopg2-binary` (used by some proxy E2E tests), and a generated Prisma client for DB-backed proxy tests, so pytest startup matches CI without manual package installs.\n\nRun specific test files:\n```bash\nuv run pytest tests/test_litellm/test_your_file.py -v\n```\n\n### Running Linting and Formatting Checks\n\nRun all linting checks (matches CI exactly):\n\n```bash\nmake lint\n```\n\nIndividual linting commands:\n```bash\nmake format-check       # Check Black formatting\nmake lint-ruff          # Run Ruff linting\nmake lint-basedpyright  # Run basedpyright type checking\nmake check-circular-imports    # Check for circular imports\nmake check-import-safety       # Check import safety\n```\n\nApply formatting (auto-fixes issues):\n```bash\nmake format\n```\n\n> **Black formatting is enforced in CI.** All PRs must pass the Black formatting check.\n>\n> - **AI coding agents** (Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, etc.): `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` instruct agents to run `poetry run black .` before committing.\n> - **VS Code users**: Install the [Black Formatter extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-python.black-formatter) and enable format-on-save:\n>   ```json\n>   {\n>     \"[python]\": {\n>       \"editor.defaultFormatter\": \"ms-python.black-formatter\",\n>       \"editor.formatOnSave\": true\n>     }\n>   }\n>   ```\n\n### CI Compatibility\n\nTo ensure your changes will pass CI, run the exact same checks locally:\n\n```bash\n# This runs the same checks as the GitHub workflows\nmake lint\nmake test-unit\n```\n\nFor exact CI compatibility (pins OpenAI version like CI):\n```bash\nmake install-dev-ci     # Installs exact CI dependencies\n```\n\n## Available Make Commands\n\nRun `make help` to see all available commands:\n\n```bash\nmake help                       # Show all available commands\nmake install-dev               # Install development dependencies\nmake install-proxy-dev         # Install proxy development dependencies\nmake install-test-deps         # Install the full local test environment\nmake format                    # Apply Black code formatting\nmake format-check              # Check Black formatting (matches CI)\nmake lint                      # Run all linting checks\nmake test-unit                 # Run unit tests\nmake test-integration          # Run integration tests\nmake test-unit-helm            # Run Helm unit tests\n```\n\n## Code Quality Standards\n\nLiteLLM follows the [Google Python Style Guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/pyguide.html).\n\nOur automated quality checks include:\n- **Black** for consistent code formatting\n- **Ruff** for linting and code quality\n- **basedpyright** for static type checking\n- **Circular import detection**\n- **Import safety validation**\n\nAll checks must pass before your PR can be merged.\n\n## Common Issues and Solutions\n\n### 1. Linting Failures\n\nIf `make lint` fails:\n\n1. **Formatting issues**: Run `make format` to auto-fix\n2. **Ruff issues**: Check the output and fix manually\n3. **basedpyright issues**: Add proper type hints\n4. **Circular imports**: Refactor import dependencies\n5. **Import safety**: Fix any unprotected imports\n\n### 2. Test Failures\n\nIf `make test-unit` fails:\n\n1. Check if you broke existing functionality\n2. Add tests for your new code\n3. Ensure tests use mocks, not real API calls\n4. Check test file naming conventions\n\n### 3. Common Development Tips\n\n- **Use type hints**: basedpyright requires proper type annotations\n- **Write descriptive commit messages**: Help reviewers understand your changes\n- **Keep PRs focused**: One feature/fix per PR\n- **Test edge cases**: Don't just test the happy path\n- **Update documentation**: If you change APIs, update docs\n\n## Building and Running Locally\n\n### LiteLLM Proxy Server\n\nTo run the proxy server locally:\n\n```bash\n# Install proxy dependencies\nmake install-proxy-dev\n\n# Start the proxy server\nuv run litellm --config your_config.yaml\n```\n\n### Docker Development\n\nIf you want to build the Docker image yourself:\n\n```bash\n# Build using the non-root Dockerfile\ndocker build -f docker/Dockerfile.non_root -t litellm_dev .\n\n# Run with your config\ndocker run \\\n    -v $(pwd)/proxy_config.yaml:/app/config.yaml \\\n    -e LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=\"sk-1234\" \\\n    -p 4000:4000 \\\n    litellm_dev \\\n    --config /app/config.yaml --detailed_debug\n```\n\n## UI Development\n\n### 1. Setup Your Local UI Development Environment\n\n```bash\n# Clone the repo (if you haven't already)\ngit clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/litellm.git\ncd litellm\n\n# Navigate to the UI dashboard directory\ncd ui/litellm-dashboard\n\n# Install dependencies\nnpm install\n\n# Start the development server\nnpm run dev\n```\n\n### 2. Adding UI Tests\n\nIf you are adding a **new component** or **new logic**, you must add corresponding tests.\n\n### 3. Running UI Unit Tests\n\n```bash\nnpm run test\n```\n\n### 4. Building the UI\n\nEnsure the UI builds successfully before submitting your PR:\n\n```bash\nnpm run build\n```\n\n## Submitting Your PR\n\n1. **Push your branch**: `git push origin your-feature-branch`\n2. **Create a PR**: Go to GitHub and open a pull request against [`litellm_internal_staging`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/litellm_internal_staging), which is the default base branch. Do not target `main`.\n3. **Fill out the PR template**: Provide clear description of changes\n4. **Wait for review**: Maintainers will review and provide feedback\n5. **Address feedback**: Make requested changes and push updates\n6. **Merge**: Once approved, your PR will be merged!\n\n## Getting Help\n\nIf you need help:\n\n- 💬 [Join our Discord](https://discord.gg/wuPM9dRgDw)\n- 💬 [Join our Slack](https://www.litellm.ai/support)\n- 📧 Email us: ishaan@berri.ai / krrish@berri.ai\n- 🐛 [Create an issue](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/new)\n\n## What to Contribute\n\nLooking for ideas? Check out:\n\n- 🐛 [Good first issues](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/labels/good%20first%20issue)\n- 🚀 [Feature requests](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/labels/enhancement)\n- 📚 Documentation improvements\n- 🧪 Test coverage improvements\n- 🔌 New LLM provider integrations\n\nThank you for contributing to LiteLLM! 🚀 \n",

document.content:
# Contributing to LiteLLM

Thank you for your interest in contributing to LiteLLM! We welcome contributions of all kinds - from bug fixes and documentation improvements to new features and integrations.

## **Checklist before submitting a PR**

Here are the core requirements for any PR submitted to LiteLLM:

- [ ] **Sign the Contributor License Agreement (CLA)** - [see details](#contributor-license-agreement-cla)
- [ ] **Keep scope isolated** - Your changes should address 1 specific problem at a time

#### Proxy (Backend) PRs

- [ ] **Add testing** - Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement - [see details](#adding-testing)
- [ ] **Ensure your PR passes all checks**:
  - [ ] [Unit Tests](#running-unit-tests) - `make test-unit`
  - [ ] [Linting / Formatting](#running-linting-and-formatting-checks) - `make lint`

#### UI PRs

- [ ] **Ensure the UI builds successfully** - `npm run build`
- [ ] **Ensure all UI unit tests pass** - `npm run test`
- [ ] **Add tests for new components or logic** - If you are adding a new component or new logic, add corresponding tests

## **Contributor License Agreement (CLA)**

Before contributing code to LiteLLM, you must sign our [Contributor License Agreement (CLA)](https://cla-assistant.io/BerriAI/litellm). This is a legal requirement for all contributions to be merged into the main repository.

**Important:** We strongly recommend reviewing and signing the CLA before starting work on your contribution to avoid any delays in the PR process.

## Quick Start

### 1. Setup Your Local Development Environment

```bash
# Fork the repository on GitHub (click the Fork button at https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm)
# Then clone your fork locally
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/litellm.git
cd litellm

# Create a new branch for your feature (see "Commit and Branch Conventions" below)
git checkout -b feature/your-feature

# Install development dependencies
make install-dev

# Install git hooks that enforce commit + branch conventions (one-time, opt-in)
make install-hooks

# Verify your setup works
make help
```

That's it! Your local development environment is ready.

## Commit and Branch Conventions

Commits follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) and branches follow [Conventional Branches](https://conventional-branch.github.io/). Run `make install-hooks` once per clone to enable the local git hooks that enforce these — see the [contributor docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code#commit-and-branch-conventions) for the full type list, examples, the protected-branch bypass list, and how to opt out.

### 2. Development Workflow

Here's the recommended workflow for making changes:

```bash
# Make your changes to the code
# ...

# Format your code (auto-fixes formatting issues)
make format

# Run all linting checks (matches CI exactly)
make lint

# Run unit tests to ensure nothing is broken
make test-unit

# Commit your changes (must follow Conventional Commits — see above)
git add .
git commit -m "feat(scope): your descriptive commit message"

# Push and create a PR (branch must follow Conventional Branches — see above)
git push origin feature/your-feature
```

## Adding Testing

**Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement for all PRs.**

### Where to Add Tests

Add your tests to the [`tests/test_litellm/` directory](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/test_litellm).

- This directory mirrors the structure of the `litellm/` directory
- **Only add mocked tests** - no real LLM API calls in this directory
- For integration tests with real APIs, use the appropriate test directories

### File Naming Convention

The `tests/test_litellm/` directory follows the same structure as `litellm/`:

- `litellm/proxy/caching_routes.py` → `tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_caching_routes.py`
- `litellm/utils.py` → `tests/test_litellm/test_utils.py`

### Example Test

```python
import pytest
from litellm import completion

def test_your_feature():
    """Test your feature with a descriptive docstring."""
    # Arrange
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
    
    # Act
    # Use mocked responses, not real API calls
    
    # Assert
    assert expected_result == actual_result
```

## Running Tests and Checks

### Running Unit Tests

Run all unit tests (uses parallel execution for speed):

```bash
make test-unit
```

If you're running broader test suites, proxy tests, or anything that touches PostgreSQL-backed fixtures/plugins, install the full local test environment first:

```bash
make install-test-deps
```

This syncs the locked test environment used across the repo, including `psycopg` v3 plus `psycopg-binary` (used by `pytest-postgresql`), `psycopg2-binary` (used by some proxy E2E tests), and a generated Prisma client for DB-backed proxy tests, so pytest startup matches CI without manual package installs.

Run specific test files:
```bash
uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/test_your_file.py -v
```

### Running Linting and Formatting Checks

Run all linting checks (matches CI exactly):

```bash
make lint
```

Individual linting commands:
```bash
make format-check       # Check Black formatting
make lint-ruff          # Run Ruff linting
make lint-basedpyright  # Run basedpyright type checking
make check-circular-imports    # Check for circular imports
make check-import-safety       # Check import safety
```

Apply formatting (auto-fixes issues):
```bash
make format
```

> **Black formatting is enforced in CI.** All PRs must pass the Black formatting check.
>
> - **AI coding agents** (Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, etc.): `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` instruct agents to run `poetry run black .` before committing.
> - **VS Code users**: Install the [Black Formatter extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-python.black-formatter) and enable format-on-save:
>   ```json
>   {
>     "[python]": {
>       "editor.defaultFormatter": "ms-python.black-formatter",
>       "editor.formatOnSave": true
>     }
>   }
>   ```

### CI Compatibility

To ensure your changes will pass CI, run the exact same checks locally:

```bash
# This runs the same checks as the GitHub workflows
make lint
make test-unit
```

For exact CI compatibility (pins OpenAI version like CI):
```bash
make install-dev-ci     # Installs exact CI dependencies
```

## Available Make Commands

Run `make help` to see all available commands:

```bash
make help                       # Show all available commands
make install-dev               # Install development dependencies
make install-proxy-dev         # Install proxy development dependencies
make install-test-deps         # Install the full local test environment
make format                    # Apply Black code formatting
make format-check              # Check Black formatting (matches CI)
make lint                      # Run all linting checks
make test-unit                 # Run unit tests
make test-integration          # Run integration tests
make test-unit-helm            # Run Helm unit tests
```

## Code Quality Standards

LiteLLM follows the [Google Python Style Guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/pyguide.html).

Our automated quality checks include:
- **Black** for consistent code formatting
- **Ruff** for linting and code quality
- **basedpyright** for static type checking
- **Circular import detection**
- **Import safety validation**

All checks must pass before your PR can be merged.

## Common Issues and Solutions

### 1. Linting Failures

If `make lint` fails:

1. **Formatting issues**: Run `make format` to auto-fix
2. **Ruff issues**: Check the output and fix manually
3. **basedpyright issues**: Add proper type hints
4. **Circular imports**: Refactor import dependencies
5. **Import safety**: Fix any unprotected imports

### 2. Test Failures

If `make test-unit` fails:

1. Check if you broke existing functionality
2. Add tests for your new code
3. Ensure tests use mocks, not real API calls
4. Check test file naming conventions

### 3. Common Development Tips

- **Use type hints**: basedpyright requires proper type annotations
- **Write descriptive commit messages**: Help reviewers understand your changes
- **Keep PRs focused**: One feature/fix per PR
- **Test edge cases**: Don't just test the happy path
- **Update documentation**: If you change APIs, update docs

## Building and Running Locally

### LiteLLM Proxy Server

To run the proxy server locally:

```bash
# Install proxy dependencies
make install-proxy-dev

# Start the proxy server
uv run litellm --config your_config.yaml
```

### Docker Development

If you want to build the Docker image yourself:

```bash
# Build using the non-root Dockerfile
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile.non_root -t litellm_dev .

# Run with your config
docker run \
    -v $(pwd)/proxy_config.yaml:/app/config.yaml \
    -e LITELLM_MASTER_KEY="sk-1234" \
    -p 4000:4000 \
    litellm_dev \
    --config /app/config.yaml --detailed_debug
```

## UI Development

### 1. Setup Your Local UI Development Environment

```bash
# Clone the repo (if you haven't already)
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/litellm.git
cd litellm

# Navigate to the UI dashboard directory
cd ui/litellm-dashboard

# Install dependencies
npm install

# Start the development server
npm run dev
```

### 2. Adding UI Tests

If you are adding a **new component** or **new logic**, you must add corresponding tests.

### 3. Running UI Unit Tests

```bash
npm run test
```

### 4. Building the UI

Ensure the UI builds successfully before submitting your PR:

```bash
npm run build
```

## Submitting Your PR

1. **Push your branch**: `git push origin your-feature-branch`
2. **Create a PR**: Go to GitHub and open a pull request against [`litellm_internal_staging`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/litellm_internal_staging), which is the default base branch. Do not target `main`.
3. **Fill out the PR template**: Provide clear description of changes
4. **Wait for review**: Maintainers will review and provide feedback
5. **Address feedback**: Make requested changes and push updates
6. **Merge**: Once approved, your PR will be merged!

## Getting Help

If you need help:

- 💬 [Join our Discord](https://discord.gg/wuPM9dRgDw)
- 💬 [Join our Slack](https://www.litellm.ai/support)
- 📧 Email us: ishaan@berri.ai / krrish@berri.ai
- 🐛 [Create an issue](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/new)

## What to Contribute

Looking for ideas? Check out:

- 🐛 [Good first issues](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/labels/good%20first%20issue)
- 🚀 [Feature requests](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/labels/enhancement)
- 📚 Documentation improvements
- 🧪 Test coverage improvements
- 🔌 New LLM provider integrations

Thank you for contributing to LiteLLM! 🚀
